data.content_ref: inline:The stated relation is 'integrates ... to suggest that genuine reliability is actually just the ability to correctly identify the world-type.' This commits to a reduction/identification (reliability = world-type identification), but the supplied REFUTED IF clause ('expert consistently outperforms a panel in a closed-world task due to higher execution speed...') never tests the identification-of-world-type claim. It tests panel-vs-expant performance and execution speed, neither of which is a property of the asserted relation (an identification/equation of reliability with world-type identification). The refutation is therefore non-substantive toward the relation it attaches to: to refute the reduction, a counterexample must show an agent that correctly identifies the world-type yet remains unreliable, or a reliable agent that fails world-type identification. The supplied clause addresses a different thesis (panel superiority) and so leaves the integration claim unrefuted.
